why: With every item moving the same way round the circle, the flow across each edge is a starting flow plus the running prefix sum of (products[i] - avg). The flows must be non-negative and the cost is their sum, so the best starting flow is minus the lowest prefix sum.
hints: Think about the number of items crossing each edge rather than individual items. How does the flow over one edge relate to the flow over the previous edge?

Going clockwise, flow out of warehouse i = flow into it + products[i] - avg. So flow_i = f + prefix_i. All flows must be >= 0 (one direction only), and cost = sum of flows, so choose f = -min(prefix_i).

One pass computing running prefix sums, their total and their minimum gives cost = total - n * min (with min including 0). Do it for the array and for its reverse (other direction) and take the smaller. O(n), 64-bit.
pitfalls: Including 0 in the minimum matters: the starting flow can't be negative.
Values up to 10^9 with n up to 10^5 overflow 32-bit integers.
Allowing both directions per edge gives the classic 'median' answer, which is smaller than what this problem allows; here each run is one-directional.
